name: Focal, Segmental or Multifocal Dystonia

criteria.description: Presence of sustained or intermittent involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal, often repetitive, movements or postures
Dystonia affecting focal, segmental, or multifocal body regions without generalized involvement
Exclusion of secondary causes such as drug-induced, structural brain lesions, or metabolic disorders
Presence of geste antagoniste (sensory trick) or task-specificity of dystonia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of involuntary muscle contractions causing dystonia in focal, segmental, or multifocal distribution with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; neuroimaging and laboratory tests are used to exclude secondary causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sustained involuntary muscle contractions causing abnormal postures
searchTerms: sustained muscle contractions causing abnormal posture
involuntary muscle tightening with odd positions
muscle spasms triggered by specific tasks

pathognomonic.symptomName: Geste antagoniste (sensory trick) ameliorating dystonic postures
searchTerms: touch or gesture reducing abnormal posture

common.symptomName: Pain associated with dystonic muscle contractions
Abnormal repetitive movements in affected body regions
Muscle spasms leading to functional impairment
Progressive spread of dystonia to adjacent body regions
searchTerms: dystonia spreading to nearby body parts

occasional.symptomName: Sensory disturbances such as paresthesia in affected limbs
searchTerms: sensory changes like pins and needles
paresthesia in affected arms or legs

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to sustained muscle contractions

searchTerms: mild muscle weakness in affected areas

occasional.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms including anxiety related to disability

searchTerms: speech problems from jaw and mouth spasms
difficulty talking due to oromandibular dystonia
speech impairment from facial muscle spasms

rare.symptomName: Dysphagia due to pharyngeal muscle involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing from throat muscle weakness
swallowing problems due to muscle involvement
breathing problems from throat muscle spasms
respiratory difficulty due to laryngeal dystonia
airway compromise from vocal cord spasms

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; used to exclude metabolic or inflammatory causes
imaging: Brain MRI typically normal; used to exclude structural lesions
genetic: Mutations in genes such as TOR1A, THAP1 may be identified in familial cases
other: Electromyography showing co-contraction of antagonist muscles during dystonic movements

redFlags: Rapid onset of dystonia with systemic symptoms
Presence of fixed structural brain lesions on imaging
History of exposure to dopamine receptor blocking agents
references: Albanese A, et al. Phenomenology and classification of dystonia: a consensus update. Mov Disord. 2013.
Marras C, et al. Dystonia: Clinical Features and Diagnosis. Neurol Clin. 2016.
